planning_range_note: Planning ranges are design defaults, not measured historical ranges. Stage 14 replaces them with ranges measured on real data. A value outside the planning range is flagged out of distribution: any result for it would be fictional exploratory.

horizon_quarters.label: Horizon
horizon_quarters.explanation: Quarters after the knowledge cutoff that a run will cover.

default_source.note: Five years, as in the API example of docs/09.

interventions.label: R&D budget change
interventions.summary: Raise or cut research and development spending.

magnitude.label: R&D change
magnitude.explanation: How much yearly R&D spending changes. A change of the budget and a change of R&D intensity are different decisions: +40% of a USD 400m budget is USD 160m a year, while +40 percentage points of a USD 4bn revenue would be USD 1.6bn.

default_source.note: A neutral starting value. The unit has no default on purpose: it changes what the number means.

parameters.label: Share capitalized
parameters.explanation: Part of the extra R&D recorded as an asset and depreciated instead of expensed at once. It moves cost from EBITDA to depreciation; the cash spent is the same.

default_source.note: US GAAP (ASC 730) expenses most R&D as incurred. Software development and some acquired R&D are exceptions.

parameters.label: Adoption delay
parameters.explanation: Time from the spending to the first revenue it could produce. The cost hits EBIT at once; any revenue comes later and is uncertain.

default_source.note: Placeholder until the causal study (Stage 20) estimates how long R&D takes to reach revenue.

share_group.label: Financing
share_group.explanation: How the cash needed for the decision is raised. Shares add up to exactly 100%; new equity dilutes existing shareholders.

default_source.note: Funded from cash on hand.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters from the effective date until spending changes.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

ramp_quarters.label: Ramp to full effect
ramp_quarters.explanation: Quarters until spending reaches the new level.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: R&D expense changes by the incremental spending, minus any capitalized share, so EBIT and EBITDA move by the same amount from the effective date.
Operating cash flow changes by the full spending; a capitalized share is reported in investing cash flow instead.
Cash falls, or debt or equity rises, by the funded amount. A capitalized share becomes an intangible asset.

interventions.does_not_mean: Higher R&D does not guarantee more revenue. Any revenue effect is an assumption with a delay, not an observed return.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).

interventions.label: Workforce restructuring

magnitude.label: Headcount change
magnitude.explanation: Change of headcount as a share of current employees. −15% means 15 of every 100 employees leave; it does not mean operating costs fall by 15%.

default_source.note: A neutral starting value for the form.

parameters.label: Payroll as a share of revenue
parameters.explanation: Turns a headcount share into dollars. Payroll means wages, salaries and benefits of all employees.

default_source.note: Total payroll is not in the demo data. Replace it with the company's own figure when known.

parameters.label: One-off cost per affected employee
parameters.explanation: Severance and restructuring charges for a reduction, or hiring and onboarding costs for an increase, in months of salary.

default_source.note: Severance depends on country, contract and seniority; this range is a placeholder.

parameters.label: Payroll change realized
parameters.explanation: Share of the gross payroll change that shows up in costs, after retention bonuses, contractors and rehiring.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

parameters.label: Productivity loss
parameters.explanation: Temporary loss of output among remaining employees during the ramp: lost knowledge, handovers, morale. It lowers revenue capacity.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

share_group.label: Financing
share_group.explanation: How the cash needed for the decision is raised. Shares add up to exactly 100%; new equity dilutes existing shareholders.

default_source.note: One-off costs paid from cash on hand.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters from the effective date until headcount changes.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

ramp_quarters.label: Ramp to full effect
ramp_quarters.explanation: Quarters until the new headcount is fully in place.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: Payroll cost changes by the realized share of the gross change. A one-off restructuring charge is recorded when the plan is committed.
Severance is paid in cash; recurring savings or costs follow payroll.
A restructuring liability is recognized and then paid, lowering cash.

interventions.does_not_mean: Cutting 15% of staff does not cut operating costs by 15%. Savings are partial, arrive with a delay and come with a one-off charge and execution risk.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).

interventions.label: Acquisition
interventions.summary: Buy another company and fund the deal.

magnitude.label: Purchase price
magnitude.explanation: Enterprise value paid for the target. The buyer does not gain the price as value: what matters is what the target earns, the synergies and the cost of funding.

default_source.note: An illustrative deal size for the form.

parameters.label: Target revenue per year
parameters.explanation: Revenue the target adds per year after closing.

default_source.note: Illustrative target. Enter the target's reported revenue.

parameters.label: Target EBITDA margin
parameters.explanation: EBITDA of the target as a share of its revenue.

default_source.note: Illustrative margin. Enter the target's own.

parameters.label: Deal costs
parameters.explanation: Advisory, legal and financing fees as a share of the purchase price. They are expensed and funded together with the price.

default_source.note: Placeholder share of the price.

parameters.label: Integration cost
parameters.explanation: One-off cost to combine systems, sites and teams, as a share of the purchase price, spread over the ramp.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

parameters.label: Cost synergies
parameters.explanation: Yearly cost savings at full integration, as a share of target revenue. They arrive at the end of the ramp, if at all.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

parameters.label: Chance the deal closes
parameters.explanation: Probability that the deal completes, for example after antitrust review. If it fails, deal costs are still spent.

default_source.note: Placeholder probability.

parameters.label: Interest rate on new debt
parameters.explanation: Annual interest rate on the debt raised for this decision.

default_source.note: Illustrative annual rate. The real rate depends on the market at the decision date and on the company's credit.

share_group.label: Financing
share_group.explanation: How the cash needed for the decision is raised. Shares add up to exactly 100%; new equity dilutes existing shareholders.

default_source.note: An illustrative even split of cash and debt.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters from the effective date until the deal closes.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

ramp_quarters.label: Ramp to full effect
ramp_quarters.explanation: Quarters of integration until synergies are complete.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: Target revenue and EBITDA are added from closing. Deal and integration costs are expensed. Interest on new debt and amortization of acquired intangibles lower net income.
The cash part of the price and the deal costs flow out at closing; new debt flows in. Synergies improve operating cash flow after the ramp.
Goodwill and acquired intangibles appear. Debt rises by the debt share; new equity dilutes existing shareholders.

interventions.does_not_mean: Paying USD 1bn does not add USD 1bn of value. Value depends on the target's cash flows, synergies, integration cost and the price of funding.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).

interventions.label: Divestiture or segment exit
interventions.summary: Sell or close part of the business.

magnitude.label: Revenue divested
magnitude.explanation: Share of the company's revenue that leaves with the sold or closed unit.

default_source.note: A neutral starting value for the form.

parameters.label: EBITDA margin of the unit
parameters.explanation: EBITDA margin of the unit that leaves. A negative margin means a loss-making unit; exiting it raises the group margin.

default_source.note: Segment figures are not in the demo data; segment reporting arrives with XBRL normalization (Stage 11).

parameters.label: Sale proceeds
parameters.explanation: Cash received from a buyer. Zero means the unit is closed.

default_source.note: Zero: a closure without a buyer.

parameters.label: Separation cost
parameters.explanation: One-off cost to separate or close the unit (contracts, systems, sites), as a share of the unit's yearly revenue.

default_source.note: Placeholder share.

parameters.label: Stranded overhead
parameters.explanation: Shared overhead that stays with the company after the unit leaves, as a share of the overhead the unit carried.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

parameters.label: Tax rate on the gain
parameters.explanation: Tax paid on the gain from a sale.

default_source.note: US federal corporate income tax rate since 2018 (Tax Cuts and Jobs Act). State taxes and the tax basis of the unit are not modelled.

share_group.label: Use of proceeds
share_group.explanation: Where the net proceeds go. Shares add up to exactly 100%.

default_source.note: An illustrative even split.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters from the effective date until the unit leaves.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.
Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: Revenue and EBITDA of the unit leave; stranded overhead stays. A gain or loss on sale and separation costs are one-off items.
Proceeds flow in, less tax on the gain and separation costs. The unit's operating cash flow stops.
The unit's assets and liabilities leave. Proceeds pay down debt, stay as cash or go to shareholders.

interventions.does_not_mean: Selling a unit with 10% of revenue does not cut costs by 10%. Shared overhead stays behind, and margins improve only if the unit earned less than the rest.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).

interventions.label: CAPEX expansion

magnitude.label: Investment
magnitude.explanation: Total capital expenditure of the program.

default_source.note: An illustrative program size for the form.

parameters.label: Capacity increase
parameters.explanation: Extra capacity as a share of current capacity. Capacity is not revenue: revenue follows only as far as the new capacity is used and sold.

default_source.note: Example from the scenario library (docs/16: new plant, +30% capacity).

parameters.label: Useful life
parameters.explanation: Years over which the investment is depreciated, straight-line.

default_source.note: Illustrative life; buildings last longer than equipment.

parameters.label: Utilization after the ramp
parameters.explanation: Share of the new capacity in use. Idle capacity still depreciates.

default_source.note: No estimate exists yet; placeholder range.

parameters.label: Interest rate on new debt
parameters.explanation: Annual interest rate on the debt raised for this decision.

default_source.note: Illustrative annual rate. The real rate depends on the market at the decision date and on the company's credit.

share_group.label: Financing
share_group.explanation: How the cash needed for the decision is raised. Shares add up to exactly 100%; new equity dilutes existing shareholders.

default_source.note: An illustrative even split of cash and debt.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters of construction before the capacity is ready.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

ramp_quarters.label: Ramp to full effect
ramp_quarters.explanation: Quarters until utilization reaches its level.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: Depreciation starts when the asset is in use. Revenue and costs from the new capacity follow utilization.
Investing cash flow falls by the investment during construction, so free cash flow drops before any return.
Property, plant and equipment rises; cash falls or debt rises.

interventions.does_not_mean: +30% capacity does not mean +30% revenue. Revenue depends on demand, price and the ramp; idle capacity is a cost.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).

interventions.label: Debt refinancing
interventions.summary: Replace existing debt with new debt.

magnitude.label: Amount refinanced
magnitude.explanation: Principal of existing debt replaced by new debt.

default_source.note: An illustrative amount for the form.

parameters.label: Current interest rate
parameters.explanation: Annual rate on the debt that is replaced.

default_source.note: Debt terms are not in the demo data. Enter the rate of the debt being replaced.

parameters.label: New interest rate
parameters.explanation: Annual rate on the new debt. Market rates at the decision date are uncertain.

default_source.note: Placeholder range.

parameters.label: New maturity
parameters.explanation: Years until the new debt must be repaid.

default_source.note: A common maturity for corporate bonds; adjust.

parameters.label: Fees
parameters.explanation: Fees and any prepayment penalty, as a share of the amount refinanced.

default_source.note: Placeholder share.

lag_quarters.label: Lag
lag_quarters.explanation: Quarters from the effective date until the new debt is drawn.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

ramp_quarters.label: Ramp to full effect
ramp_quarters.explanation: Quarters until all old debt is replaced.

default_source.note: Typical timing for this kind of decision; adjust it.

mechanism.effect: Interest expense changes by the amount times the rate difference. Fees and any write-off of old issuance costs are one-off.
Interest payments change; fees are paid at closing. Principal is replaced.
Debt stays about the same; its rate and maturity change.

interventions.does_not_mean: A lower rate does not create value by itself if fees, a shorter maturity or covenants offset it. Past rates were set by the market, not chosen by the company.
interventions.evidence: Unsupported hypothetical. No causal estimate exists for this decision type yet; the causal pipeline (Stage 20) studies R&D intensity first (decision D-03).
